cells.tense: You are here, at the clearing, and you are not rushing it to be finished.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're keeping out of habit and put it down today, then stop there — let the ending be done.
cells.core:
You're in the middle of something ending, and you're not forcing it to be over before it is. Enough light to take the next step, not the whole road — and that's fine, because you're actually walking it. The dream you're dreaming comes from what you've already lived through, which is why it holds weight instead of floating. When you imagine what's next, it's built on something real.

This balance isn't a resting place. The clearing is still going on, and there's more to carry out. Feed it with one thing you do on purpose — a direction you choose because you want it, not because the ruins are still asking. What you're free to feed next is momentum you actually picked.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting something end, and you're not forcing the next thing yet.
cells.verb: moving through uncertainty without forcing it to resolve

cells.tense: You are living ahead of the ending, in a future you keep trying to write before it arrives.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're already treating as over, and do nothing about it for a day except notice it's still here.
cells.core:
You're in a clearing, but you're living in the version after it — rehearsing what comes next, imagining the shape of a life that isn't here yet. The dream has gotten vivid enough that it's competing with the room you're standing in. You keep reaching for the next chapter before this one has actually ended.

What steadies this isn't dreaming less and it isn't forcing yourself into the present. It's care aimed at what's actually growing instead of what might grow — small, patient, unhurried. Put your hands on something real and tend that, no outcome promised. Care that doesn't exhaust is the opposite of clutching at a future that hasn't arrived. Whatever you tend today is enough.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed and refusing to look at what it was.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about something that's ending, out loud, and let that be the whole act — no plan after it.
cells.core:
Something ended, and you're treating it as a fact to get past rather than a thing to feel. No depth, no dream, just the plain surface of it — and that flatness keeps the clearing from finishing. When something endings-shaped comes up, you reach for the literal reading and move on. The not-knowing feels like a threat instead of a place you could stand.

It isn't imagination that's missing. It's the direct knowing that something is over, without needing to explain it. Trust one perception about what's clearing, without arguing it into a case. You don't have to feel your way through anything. Just let one thing land as true, and let that be enough for today.

cells.tense: You are already shaping what comes next, in a room you don't realize you're writing.
cells.ask: Write one sentence about what you want next, keep it where you'll see it, and read it once tomorrow.
cells.core:
You're imagining a life past this clearing, and you'd say you're just being realistic. But the pictures you keep running — what you'll do, who you'll be — are steering choices you're making right now. The dreaming is happening. You haven't said so. You'd call it practical thinking, if you called it anything.

What brings it back is smaller than vision. A practice, kept by attention, not a flash. One sentence, written and revisited. Solitude here connects rather than isolates, because you're actually meeting what you want instead of letting it run you. Refinement that serves growth, not the need to get it right. What you write down is yours — the rest is noise.
